mitre_tactics.name: File and Directory Discovery
mitre_tactics.justification: File and Directory Discovery (Discovery) — File system enumerated to identify valuable data, credentials, or configuration files. Technique ID mapped from threat intelligence corpus.

mitre_tactics.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
mitre_tactics.justification: Command and Scripting Interpreter (Execution) — Adversary abuses command-line or scripting interpreters to execute malicious code. Technique ID mapped from threat intelligence corpus.

ttps.justification: Technique applies because: directory traversal. The File and Directory Discovery technique is relevant because this vulnerability's attack mechanism aligns with Discovery phase behavior (analyst inference from advisory text).
ttps.observed_behavior: NOT OBSERVED. Hypothesis from the vulnerability description: exploiting 'ZDI-26-752: (0Day) Genesis World decompress_usdz Directory Traversal Remote Code' could enable File and Directory Discovery (T1083) in the Discovery phase. No adversary use of this technique is reported by the source.
ttps.detection_hint: Alert on ../ patterns in web request URLs. Monitor for access to sensitive directories (/etc/passwd, /proc, windows/system32). Alert on LFI/RFI patterns.
ttps.kql_example: DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteUrl has_any ('../','..%2F','..%5C','/etc/passwd','/proc/self')

ttps.justification: Technique applies because: code execution. The Command and Scripting Interpreter technique is relevant because this vulnerability's attack mechanism aligns with Execution phase behavior (analyst inference from advisory text).
ttps.observed_behavior: NOT OBSERVED. Hypothesis from the vulnerability description: exploiting 'ZDI-26-752: (0Day) Genesis World decompress_usdz Directory Traversal Remote Code' could enable Command and Scripting Interpreter (T1059) in the Execution phase. No adversary use of this technique is reported by the source.
ttps.detection_hint: Monitor for unusual parent-child process relationships. Alert on PowerShell with encoded commands, downloading content, or disabling security features.
ttps.kql_example: DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ('IEX','Invoke-Expression','-EncodedCommand','DownloadString','bypass')
